title: Coordinated cutover and fallback playbook: runtime + control plane migration
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for coordinating a combined runtime + control-plane migration for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Goal: zero-to-minimal user impact, predictable rollback, and clear Terraform/module steps for infra teams. This doc covers pre-cutover validation, staged cutover with traffic shifting, compatibility shims, and explicit rollback recipes.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: private-deployments clusters running Redwood Runtime vX.Y -> vX+1.Z and Control Plane vA.B -> vA+1.C in the same maintenance window.
- Databases: Postgres (control plane state) and Redis/KV for caches.
- Networking: Envoy/ASG or equivalent for traffic shifting.
- Terraform: state in S3/GCS with locking; modules used: rfv_private_cluster, rfv_controlplane, rfv_runtime.
- A/B testing tooling: weighted routing via control-plane route rules or LB weight adjustments.
- All actions must be coordinated over #infra-deployments and the on-call SRE.

Roles and contacts:
- Migration lead: Marcus Riley (owner)
- Runtime lead: Ava Chen
- Control-plane lead: Priya Kapoor
- Terraform/Infra: Diego Martinez
- SRE on-call: rotation (see Slack pinned roster)
- Customer success / impacted stakeholders: list in linked_artifacts

High-level strategy:
1) Prepare: build and validate new artifacts (containers, packages, tf plan) in staging and a dedicated canary cluster.
2) Canary: deploy control plane and runtime to canary namespace; shift 1-3% of traffic. Monitor for regressions.
3) Gradual ramp: move traffic in controlled steps (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) with validation windows and automated guards.
4) Cutover complete: finalize configs, run post-migration validation, and clean compatibility shims after 48+ hours.
5) Rollback plan: graded rollback (quick fail-stop for severe breaks, graceful fallback for functional regressions).

Prerequisites checklist (must be green before cutover):
- [ ] Terraform plans reviewed and stored in artifact storage (tagged).
- [ ] Smoke test suite pass for runtime and control plane images in staging.
- [ ] E2E test harness with synthetic prompts and baseline metrics for p50/p95 latency and token-acceptance.
- [ ] DB backup (logical + physical snapshot) and verified restore on a sandbox.
- [ ] Snapshot of all Terraform state and a separate copy in 'rollback-artifacts/'.
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards copied and pinned for this migration (latency, error-rate, GPU-util, token/sec).
- [ ] Feature flags and API-compat shims available and toggles validated.
- [ ] Communication plan: status page template, stakeholder email, #infra-deployments message cadence.

Version compatibility matrix (example):
- Control plane vA.B (current) -> vA+1.C (target): API surface changes: new route param 'prefer_variant', optional. Backwards compatible when unset.
- Runtime vX.Y -> vX+1.Z: Model handler API adds endpoint /v2/kv-cache/warmup; runtime continues to accept /v1/prompt for backward compatibility.
- Terraform modules: rfv_runtime v2 -> v3 (module refactor: split runtime_compute and runtime_config). Ensure import/rename steps below.

Terraform-specific notes and tactics:
- Workspaces: use isolated workspace per environment (tf workspace select prod-mig-20250110).
- State Import: when module names change (rfv_runtime v2 -> v3), use 'terraform state mv' to move resources into new module structure before applying changes. Record commands in rollback-artifacts.
- Locking: ensure state locking via DynamoDB/etcd for the duration of the operation. Only 1 operator may apply at a time.
- Plan review process: attach tfplan artifact to JIRA ticket and include diff summary in the deployment doc.
- Partial apply: prefer multiple smaller plans (control-plane first, then runtime) to reduce blast radius.
- Example commands:
  - terraform workspace new prod-mig-20250110 || terraform workspace select prod-mig-20250110
  - terraform plan -out=tfplan-controlplane -var-file=prod.tfvars
  - terraform apply tfplan-controlplane

Pre-cutover staging validation (detailed):
- Canary cluster deployment (namespaces: canary-ctrl, canary-runtime).
- Run the full regression suite (tests tagged 'migration-smoke') -> must pass 3 consecutive runs across 2 days.
- API compatibility tests: call old clients (v1 SDK) and new clients (v2 SDK) and verify identical responses for 100 sample prompts.
- KV warmup validation: call /v2/kv-cache/warmup on the new runtime and measure reduction in first-token latency for hot prefixes.
- Chaos test: simulate node restart and network partition within canary to validate graceful fallback to alternate region.

Canary cutover procedure:
1. Deploy control plane target version to canary namespace (do not take over full cluster control plane).
2. Deploy runtime target version to canary runtime pool.
3. Run smoke tests (health, basic generation, embeddings).
4. Shift 1% traffic: set route weight or LB weight to point 1% to canary. Example: envoy weight command or update route config via control-plane API.
5. Monitor for 30 minutes for the following: error-rate increases >0.5pp, p95 latency regression >30%, increase in model hallucination rate per eval harness.
6. If green, increment to 10% and repeat; maintain rollback ready state for 10 minutes after each increment.

Full cutover staged rollout (recommended ramp):
- 0 -> 1% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%
- Stabilization windows: 30m, 45m, 1h, 2h, 4h between steps respectively (adjust for org policy).
- Automate guard checks with a small script that queries Prometheus and fails the step if thresholds are exceeded.

Automated guard examples (pseudocode):
- if (error_rate_delta > 0.005) fail_step
- if (p95_latency_ratio > 1.30) fail_step
- if (gpu_util > 95% for 10m) alert and throttle

API compatibility shims and adapter layer guidance:
- If control-plane introduces new optional fields, keep the runtime tolerant (ignore unknown fields).
- Provide an API-adapter sidecar (lightweight proxy) that can rewrite incoming requests for legacy clients when strict validation is enforced upstream. Deploy the adapter to the canary first.
- Document new response fields as 'opt-in' via header X-Redwood-Features: v2

KV / cache migration specifics:
- Strategy: dual-populate cache for 48 hours (write-through to both old and new cache keys).
- Warm-up: replay top N prefixes via synthetic workload (script included in linked_artifacts).
- Validation: track cold-start latency percentile and cache hit ratio. Expect hit ratio to rise above baseline within 2 hours.

Database schema migration (safe pattern):
- Use expand-then-contract: deploy schema additions as nullable or new tables first, migrate reads/writes in app via feature flag, then backfill, and finally drop old fields.
- For any destructive change, schedule a maintenance window and take DB lock snapshot + logical dumps.

Rollback and fallback playbooks (explicit):
- Immediate rollback (severe outage - >30% error rate or sustained >2x p95 latency for 30m):
  1) Stop traffic to target version: set route weight 100% -> previous version.
  2) If Terraform introduced infra changes that are incompatible, run 'terraform apply' against rollback-autobackup plan stored in rollback-artifacts.
  3) Revert control-plane config by redeploying the last-known-good image: kubectl set image deployment/control-plane control-plane=redwood/control-plane:vA.B --namespace=production
  4) Re-deploy runtime LKG image and restart pods: kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime --namespace=production OR kubectl set image deployment/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:vX.Y
  5) Notify stakeholders and open an incident with severity mapping.
- Graceful rollback (functional regression only):
  1) Flip feature flags off for affected features.
  2) Use API adapter sidecar to emulate legacy behavior for affected customer tokens.
  3) Pause further ramp and run targeted fixes in canary.

Post-cutover validation (first 24h):
- Run the full synthetic evaluation harness every 2h for 24h and compare against baseline.
- Verify token accounting and billing events for first 24h for anomalies.
- Ensure error budgets remain within target.
- Confirm all telemetry (trace IDs) are present and searchable in APM.

Observability and signals to watch (priority order):
1) Client-facing error rate by route (5m and 1h)
2) Latency p50, p95, p99 for generation endpoints
3) Throughput (tokens/sec) and queue depth metrics
4) GPU utilization and model OOMs/errors
5) Control-plane error/instrumentation counts (deployment hooks failing)
6) Cache hit ratios and first-token latency for warmed prefixes

Incident triage template (use when rollback triggered):
- Time of trigger:
- Step in rollout where triggered:
- Exact guard that tripped (metric + threshold):
- Action taken (weights reverted, terraform rollback applied):
- Current mitigation state (traffic %, degraded regions):
- Next steps and owners:

Clean-up and retrospective:
- After 48–72 hours and when stable, remove API shims and adapter sidecars.
- Delete canary namespaces and unused tf workspaces.
- Collect artifacts: tfplans, kubectl rollout history, monitoring snapshots, incident timeline.
- Run a blameless postmortem and attach to JIRA ticket.

Appendix: small checklist for on-call at each step (quick reference):
- Verify pre-cutover checklist green
- Lock Terraform state and communicate write window
- Deploy control-plane to canary -> run smoke tests -> 1% traffic
- Monitor for 30m, if green -> increment traffic per ramp plan
- If guard trips -> run rollback playbook (immediate or graceful)

Notes and known pitfalls (from past migrations):
- Module renames without state-move cause long recoveries; always 'terraform state mv' during maintenance window.
- KV warmup scripts should throttle to avoid saturating GPUs during ramp.
- Backward-compatiblity mismatches are usually validation schema changes; maintain tolerant parsing and keep old SDKs supported for at least 2 minor releases.

Contact log and audit trail guidance:
- Log all terraform apply commands with username and tfplan hash in the migration ticket.
- Record exact image digests (not tags) for all deployed artifacts.
- Keep all rollback artifacts (tfplan, previous images, DB snapshots) in rollback-artifacts/ with timestamps.

Open items (TODOs):
- [ ] Add customer-specific rollback runbooks for top 5 enterprise customers.
- [ ] Automate guard-check script and include it in infra repo.
- [ ] Add runbook snippet for on-prem air-gapped installs (image transfer steps).

End of draft.

If you are on execution duty, copy this doc to a deployment ticket, attach TF plan artifacts, and leave a comment in #infra-deployments when you start the operation.
